title: :export ICSS rule
impact: Most-demanded missing CSS modules feature: 8 reactions on the issue, 8 on the use-case comment, ~10 users across 2023-2026. Main source is Sass users exposing $variables to JS (`:export { rows: $rows }`), a pattern documented by css-loader/webpack and common in CRA-era codebases. Users hit it when Vite (css.transformer: 'lightningcss', Vite 8/rolldown) or Next.js/Turbopack route CSS modules through Lightning CSS; one commenter switched Vite back to esbuild over it.
code: src/selector.rs: SelectorParser::parse_non_ts_pseudo_class (':export' becomes PseudoClass::Custom with a generic warning)
src/rules/style.rs / src/stylesheet.rs: where a top-level :export rule would be collected and removed
summary: With cssModules on, `:export { rowCount: 4 }` is not recognized: the block is copied into the output CSS unchanged, nothing is added to `exports`, and the only signal is a misleading warning ("'export' is not recognized as a valid pseudo-class. Did you mean '::export'..."). No error even in strict mode, so the breakage is silent at build time and shows up as `undefined` in JS. The docs list :import/:export as unsupported.
repro: 404-repro.mjs. Input `:export { rowCount: 4; primaryColor: #ff0000; } .list { color: red }` with cssModules:true -> output keeps `:export {...}` verbatim, exports = {list} only, warning about unknown pseudo-class. Same on local, 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1, 1.30.0, 1.27.0.
evidence: repro.mjs on local + 1.27.0..1.33.0; feature case WRONG everywhere, controls correct. Docs website/pages/css-modules.md 'Unsupported features' lists :import/:export. ICSS spec: github.com/css-modules/icss. Not a CSS standard.

fix.approach: Philosophy fit: unlike @value, `:export` is valid CSS syntax (a style rule with an unknown pseudo-class and custom-ident declarations) and only appears inside the already-supported cssModules mode, so it needs no tokenizer/parser extension or per-property substitution. Implement as: in cssModules mode, a top-level rule whose selector is exactly `:export` is removed from the output and each declaration `name: <tokens>` is added to exports. API shape: putting the serialized value in the existing `name` field ({rowCount: {name: '4', composes: [], isReferenced: false}}) would make Vite/Parcel/Turbopack expose it with no downstream changes, but overloads `name`; a separate field/kind is cleaner but changes the exports shape. Cheap interim step regardless: a specific error/warning ('ICSS :export is not supported') instead of the '::export' suggestion.

notVerified: Did not verify which Vite 8 / Next.js configurations route CSS modules through Lightning CSS by default (Vite's default css.transformer may still be postcss, in which case postcss-modules consumes :export before minification). Did not check how Turbopack maps exports to JS.
